utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar, and good morning, everybody. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record, all the accused are here. From amongst the Defence teams, I only notice the absence of Mr. Haynes and Ms. Condon. The Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey -- and also Mr. Meek. The Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. That's it. Witness and Magistrate and Legal Assistant and Registrar, Madam Registrar, I welcome you back. We shall continue now with the testimony. Witness, may I just remind you of two things before you start. First is that you are still testifying pursuant to your solemn declaration of yesterday, and second is you are reminded of your rights against self-incrimination that I explained to you yesterday. Having said that, I will now leave you in the hands of Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to the witness and to His Honour, the Magistrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you just confirm for me because I haven't heard your voice yet this morning, I am not sure I am receiving the signal from (redacted), and I am on the right channel. Can you just confirm you can hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please try to be careful, being careful even in avoiding certain courtesy. Mr. Lazarevic, we will redact that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I became aware of it the moment I it, but, unfortunately, it was too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry, it happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to continue where we left off yesterday, and I would like to pick up just one detail I noticed on the record. Speaking on page 21 of yesterday's transcript --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are not getting the translation of the questions by Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will check that immediately. We have a technical problem, Witness. The reporter is not receiving translation of Mr. Lazarevic's words. Mr. Lazarevic, can I ask you to say something again in your own language?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you hear me loud and clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems we have resolved this little hitch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, since there was no interpretation, I'll have to ask the same question again. We are now talking about the event when you left the Jahorina Centre to Srebrenica; and speaking of page 21, line 1 of yesterday's transcript, you said that you had been informed you were going to Potocari. You will agree with me that, actually, when you left Mount Jahorina, nobody told you specifically you are going to Potocari. They actually told you, you were heading for the area of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That probably would be right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what I assumed. I just wanted to clear up that detail. Also in yesterday's evidence, page 21, lines 3 to 5, you said that before leaving for Srebrenica, you and your colleagues from the Jahorina Centre were addressed by somebody higher than Jevic. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As I was looking at the statement you gave to the Prosecution - that's 7D00645, for the record - on page 6 in the B/C/S version, I found - and it's page 6 in English as well - you said that the person who addressed you at that time was the commander of all special units. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- to be quite honest with you, no, but I'm sure that it was a higher rank than Mr. Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can refresh your memory by quoting that passage from your statement. It's page 6: "A man who was introduced to us as the commander of all special police forces of Republika Srpska addressed a speech to us. I saw him for the first and the last time." Does this help you recall this part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it on my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you, the officer was introduced to us as the highest-ranking officer; and, at this stage, I cannot recall what was his full rank, but he was definitely, by the looking of Mr. Jevic, how he was addressing the gentleman, that he was addressing, that gentleman was a higher-ranking officer than Mr. Jevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Would there be any reason for you to change this part of this statement at this moment and to say that he was not actually the commander of all special police forces? Would you change this part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the sense that you would no longer testify that that man was the commander of all special police forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I cannot properly remember at this stage, I wouldn't like to change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just one more question with regard to this gentleman. To the best of your recollection, could you please describe him, that man who is the commander of all special units, how old he was, his build, the colour of his hair, his face, anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you, I cannot recollect the image of the gentleman because it was a brief visit. It was really in a short period of time, and we have had been still in a shock in the past happening. And we just -- I just could not recall that gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Of course, I won't insist if you can't remember. Before that gentleman addressed you, the commander of all special units, and Jevic as well, had anyone at the centre ever mentioned the possibility of your going to Srebrenica? In other words, before this, did you know you were going to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [In English] Your Honours, I heard the witness saying "no" very -- oh, now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you testified yesterday on page 21, lines 18 and 19 of the transcript, you said you had all assembled, boarded the buses, and left. Do you recall that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, in your statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor - and that's on page 6 in B/C/S and page 7 of the English - you stated to the Prosecution that (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And to refresh your memory, I will quote the passage to you: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just ask my friend to read the next sentence from this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, I believe that -- by all means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Continued: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I've just read this entire paragraph, but I'm only interested in this first detail. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that day, in the afternoon, you arrived at Bilalovac village, the Bratunac municipality. You put up at the schoolhouse and continued the next day. Is that the gist of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that night, when you were at the schoolhouse in Bilalovac village, can you recall whether a certain member -- a certain number of the members of your unit escaped, ran a wall across the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there has been few escapes, but did it happen the first night? I cannot recall it at this stage. But there has been one or two escapes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Generally speaking, would you agree with me that your unit, that is, the Jahorina Centre Unit, was not well prepared or well trained enough for any serious action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood your evidence correctly, practically all members of your unit were brought from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the Republika Srpska against their will.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to the following day. Sometime around 9.00 in the morning, you took the road from the place we have discussed so far across the Yellow Bridge in the direction of Potocari, and you said it took you two to three hours to reach Potocari. So I conclude that you arrived approximately around noon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could I take you back to the moment when you were leaving from Zuti Most, the Yellow Bridge. Speaking about that yesterday, you mentioned there was a Dutch check-point there. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have heard a lot of evidence about these events; and just to familiarise you a bit, we used to refer to this point as the Dutch observation point "Papa." So when I say "Papa," I will refer to the Dutch observation post near the Yellow Bridge. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On your way to Potocari, you passed by the Observation Post Papa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Passing by that observation post, did there occur any hostilities between your unit and the Dutch soldiers manning that post? Did you open fire at them? Did they open fire at you? Was there any exchange of threats? Any kind of hostility whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in assuming that had there occurred any shooting at the Dutch observation post, or had they shot at you, that would certainly be something you would remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on, your unit reached the Dutch base, where you saw Dutch troops. The Dutch soldiers that you saw, can you confirm that some of them were in full combat gear; whereas, others were wearing shorts and T-shirts only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As your unit wasn't sufficiently well trained, straightaway upon your arrival in Potocari, you scattered around the area, and it was only after a certain amount of time had gone by that you succeeded in rallying your ranks again and deploy; is that what happened? Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just clarify that question for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. On page 7 of your statement, it's 7 in the B/C/S and also 7 in the English version. Speaking about these events, you said the following: "We were not a well-trained group, and we scattered around as soon as we arrived." Do you stand by that statement, as you gave it to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. (redacted) (redacted) And you said more or less that you did nothing special, but I'd like to ask you about one detail there. You had communication with members of the Dutch Battalion. Did you talk to those soldiers? Did you socialise a little with them that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And one more thing for the record, so that we can have that clarified. From that place where you were then -- or rather, let me put it this way: From the place you were, you couldn't see the asphalt road passing by the base, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in distance. It was not in a close vicinity, but I could see -- I could not see it, virtually, but I could see the vehicles in distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to ask you a couple of questions now in relation to the members of the Dutch Battalion over there. Did anybody order you to disarm the members of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you didn't do that at your own initiative, I mean, you or members of your unit, your colleagues from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were told to us, but, sir, I can only speak on my behalf and the events that happened to me and what orders, if any, I've been given. I cannot speak for anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, but you didn't hear any order given that the members of the Dutch Battalion should be disarmed, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me [Realtime transcript read in error "to me"].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. One moment, because the last line of the transcript may be misleading. I distinctly heard the witness say, "No, not me," but the transcript says, "No, not to me." At this point, particularly, the obvious reason why the question was put by Mr. Lazarevic, I think we need to correct that, but I stand to be corrected by the witness if I am not right, if I am not correct. The question to you was whether you heard any order given, not necessarily to you, but maybe to others that the members of the Dutch Battalion should be disarmed. Did you hear any such order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Now, my next question is this: Did you, by threat of weapons or in any other way, prevent the members of the Dutch Battalion from leaving the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps have any such order to prevent them from leaving the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my best recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And just one more question with respect to this: Did you personally have an order to separate the military-able men, Muslims, from their families in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, no, I haven't, and I haven't seen any of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. According to your testimony, you remained in Potocari roughly up until 9.00 or 10.00 in the evening. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my best recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Speaking before this Tribunal yesterday - and that is on page 37 of the transcript, lines 18 and 19 - you said that you think that you were in Potocari on the 13th of July, or rather, that it could have been between the 13th and 15th of July. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And further on, on that same page of the transcript, you said that you, in fact, believe that you left Jahorina on the 13th of July and that you arrived in Potocari, in fact, on the 14th of July. That's on the same page of the transcript. Do you remember having said that, that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I did say as well that I'm not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood it, too. Now, before this Court, we had an occasion to -- we have had occasion to hear many testimonies and to see many documents, from which we can see that the evacuation of civilians from Potocari lasted for two days, that is to say, on the 12th and 13th of July, and that it was completed only on the 13th of July in the afternoon. I'd like now to go through your statement again and try to determine the time, where you were exactly, during those two days. On page 8 - and that is the Prosecution statement that I'm referring to now. It is 8 in the B/C/S version and 9 of the English version - you say that on that day when you were in Potocari, you assumed that all the people had been evacuated because you did not notice a single refugee when you were moving around, nor did you hear anything unusual. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you confirm that that is correct; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my best knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could just have some clarification about the time of the day, and I think that is in that part of the statement, and that just might help with where exactly we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Then I will read the whole paragraph just for my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I left Potocari between 2100 hours and 2200 hours. We all gathered in front of the compound, where we stayed for about half an hour, and then left the area by bus. I assumed that all the people had been evacuated because I did not see any refugee, nor did I hear anything special." [In English] Does this satisfy my colleague's inquiry?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It does. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we've just read out that entire paragraph. I certainly did not wish to disorient you in any way by just showing you a portion of that. It speaks for itself, but my question to you is the following: Had it happened that in Potocari, at that point in time when you set out, had there been ten or more thousand refugees, you would certainly have had to have noticed that; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that vicinity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. And would you agree with me when I say that on that day, regardless, of course, of the date that that was, when in the evening hours you left Potocari, that the evacuation of the population had already been completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A large number of exhibits have been presented before this Tribunal, showing that the evacuation of the civilians had been completed by the 13th of July. Now, would you agree with me, then, that the date of your stay in Potocari could have been precisely that day, the 13th of July, when the evacuation was over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be, but my belief is we went in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine. We won't pursue the point. Testifying yesterday before this Tribunal, you spoke about the White House, Bila Kuca; and looking at the transcript carefully, I noticed that this "Bila Kuca" was written in inverted commas, and it's page 40, line 1 to 2. Where did you get this term "White House" when you asked about the house you saw? How did you come to term it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A photo has been shown to me when I had been giving the statement about the house, and I did recognise the house in a photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you told at the time that it was the White House?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, the house was in white colour, so it's normal to be a white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there are many houses that are white. Why did you select this term, personally, "The White House"? You could have just said it's that house. Why did you term it that way, "the White House"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did confirm that the house that I did mention in my testimony is the house that I have seen. I don't recall coming to the term, but the house is the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Witness, and one moment, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I really don't want to continue to intervene, but I notice that at page 14, line 7 - and I didn't want to interrupt this discussion about the White House; I wanted to let that finish - it appears that the witness, from the transcript, didn't finish his answer. I believe I did hear an answer. I obviously don't want to say what I thought I heard, but I would ask if the witness could complete the answer or if he had more to say to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me check with you. Line 7 is our line 7. What do you have in your line 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just pardon me. It just scrolled up. I need to freeze it for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, because I believe you're referring to line 3 and not line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In our transcript, the previous question was: "Now, would you agree with me, then, that the date of your stay in Potocari could be precisely that day, the 13th of July, when the evacuation was over?" The answer is: "It might be, but my belief is we went in --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And so we're speaking of page 14, line 3 and not line 7. Witness, I don't know if you have been following. You were asked the following question by Mr. Lazarevic: "A large number of exhibits have been presented before this Tribunal, showing that the evacuation of the civilians had been completed by the 13th of July. Now, would you agree with me, then, that the date of your stay in Potocari could have been precisely that day, the 13th of July, when the evacuation was over?" Now, according to our transcript, we have an unfinished sentence. I did hear you complete it, but it doesn't show in the transcript. You said: "It might be, but my belief is that we went in --" Could you complete that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That we went in first. I meant that we were the first unit that actually came into the area of the Dutch compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Lazarevic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, after that digression, let's go back to the subject of the White House, if that's no problem. As far as I understood it yesterday, understood your testimony yesterday, my colleague Mr. Thayer asked you where, in relation to the base, the United Nations base, was that White House. And your answer was that as far as you remember, it was on the other side of the road. Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's just clarify the answer you gave to Mr. Thayer. Was it a house that was immediately across from the UNPROFOR base, the entrance to the UNPROFOR base on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's try and help you with that. In the statement you gave to the investigators of the Prosecution, and this is to be found on page 8 of the B/C/S and also on page 8 of the English text, you say the following: "I came across Jevic. He was standing in front of the house which was directly across the entrance to the base." Does that refresh your memory, that it was directly opposite the entrance to the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that's correct, is it, what I've just quoted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my best knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As we've cleared that up now, let's move on. The next day, you were free. You spent your time in the school in Bilalovac. And in the afternoon, you were deployed along the road between Kravica and Konjevic Polje, that communication line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on that road, to the best of your recollections, you stayed for four or five days; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd like now -- we're talking about that first day which you spent on the road. Well, yesterday you testified about the fact that on that day, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. I don't see any difference in substance, and please believe me that it wasn't my intention to say that you agreed with me about something that you did not think the same way as I did. But from this answer, too, I can conclude that (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the deposition you gave in your country of residence, I found, on page 22 in B/C/S and page 26 in English, that on the next day you found out -- (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just clear up now one more thing that remained ambivalent in your testimony yesterday? You already confirmed that on that road, you spent some four or five days. Could you now just tell me, did you spend the nights on the road as well or did you perhaps go to the schoolhouse to sleep in Bilalovac or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had been there 24 hours, day and night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clear now. It wasn't quite clear from the record yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From this answer, I conclude that you would probably be unable to tell us his name, surname, date of birth, place of residence, or any detail that could help identify him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that one of your colleagues from the training centre at Jahorina, his colleague [Realtime transcript read in error "a woman"] was wounded. Having reviewed the record, I believe some things remained insufficiently clear, so can I take you back to this event. I will lead you by my questions so that we can establish a time line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There is one correction for the transcript. It's on page 22, line 7. It says "a woman was wounded," and actually I said his colleague was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you know also if his colleague was a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can make a wild guess that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Let's correct that. I mean, that will be corrected in due course, Mr. Lazarevic. Let's proceed, please. Thank you. Let's proceed please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us try to establish a timeline. One Muslim fighter came out, saying he wanted to surrender; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As he was approaching your colleague from the Jahorina Training Centre, instead of surrendering, that fighting man, or as you said, you are not sure how to term him, threw a hand grenade at your colleague, wounding him; after which, your colleague remained an invalid, remained disabled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did throw the grenade, and a colleague was wounded, and we have heard later, when the ambulance took him, that he remained severely disabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you now remember, roughly, where on that road this incident took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, (redacted) towards the Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Right. I suppose that if you were at a distance of 100 metres, you were able to hear the explosion loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From your testimony yesterday, on page 55 of the transcript, I understood that you heard about prisoners being liquidated in Kravica several days after being placed on that road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during that five-day stay on the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Right. And this was second-hand information. You did not see that personally. You were not there. You heard about it from other members of your unit, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If you can recall, could you give us the name, surname, nickname, place of residence of any member of your unit who might have told you about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the way back, after your deployment on the road, you passed by the warehouse in Kravica. You were able to see it, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you also passed it on the way to the road to be deployed. You could see it then as well, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but I didn't pay attention to anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. If I can just try to remind you of certain details, because I suppose you were not paying attention to that in particular. But in your statement given to the OTP, on page 12 in B/C/S, page 13 in English, you said that you did not notice anything special about the warehouse, and the traces that were visible were old and greyish. Does that help you remember what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that was the case. There was nothing on the facade of that warehouse that would indicate that something unusual, out of the ordinary, had happened inside. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have some questions related to your status in July 1995. Have you ever received an official ID from the Ministry of the Interior, the MUP, of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nor did you receive the policeman's badge that is also a kind of ID, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nor did you ever conclude a contract, an employment contract, with the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nor did you receive any kind of written document, such as a decision confirming that you were admitted into the police force of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question on this topic before we look at a document. In your military service book, was the time you spent in the training centre in Jahorina entered? Maybe I should have asked you first whether there were entries made at all in your service book, but could you answer this one, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer. I think you have the same concerns that I have. Should we be in open session for this or should we be in closed session, because I think this area of the witness's testimony was covered in private session yesterday. Please check me out, but that's my recollection. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. President. And you're probably on top of this, but we have some redactions that I think we'll need to make in the transcript already on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. And are you proceeding on this part of your questions or this area of cross-examination or are you finished with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, I just have a couple of more questions in this respect, then I would ask to have our break a bit earlier just to consult, then I will have additionally ten to 15 minutes, and then that would conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But I believe we should proceed in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I was going to confirm. So let's go into private session for a while, please, and someone will go through the latter part of the transcript to establish what redactions need to be made.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will take the break now, Mr. Lazarevic, during which you can consult with your client. Twenty-five minutes. We'll have the usual break for 25 minutes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic, have you consulted with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I did, Your Honour, and I will have just five or ten minutes more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And before I proceed, I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to page 2, line 2 of the transcript, because there it says that today's witness is "PW-108," and it's actually "PW-100." And I believe it should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it would be wise to move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then let's do that. Let's move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall receiving any information as to the location where the 2nd Company, commanded by Mr. Nedzo Ikonjic was deployed during the period time you were deployed on that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the rumour had it that they had been in the area of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And to your recollection, sir, were there any members of the 2nd Company under Mr. Ikonjic along the stretch of road where you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, earlier today you were asked by my learned friend about a statement or a portion of your statement where you described being dispersed or scattered in Potocari when you first arrived. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to refer -- well, do you recall whether you were ever regrouped prior to being deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please rephrase that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. You described being dispersed or scattered upon your arrival at Potocari. Were you ever deployed in any particular fashion around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few soldiers or a few Jahorina guys have been deployed in some sort of military fashion around the compound, yes, and I was one of them that has been dispersed around the compound, actually put on the position. It was, I believe, about eight or nine of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked some questions about the dates on which these events occurred. Do you recall being asked some questions about the dates in your deposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably was asked the dates, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you recall, sitting here today, what your answers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what those -- can you tell the Trial Chamber what your answers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. My answer was: I believe it was either 12th or 13th of July, maybe even 14th. I'm not sure, but my honest belief is that we are the very first unit that actually has entered Potocari. If that date of entry of Potocari is noted as the 12th, then I firmly believe it was the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I want to show you a document, and it is on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'll leave it up to our technical people to decide whether it's better to show it on e-court or on the ELMO. It is a hospital record for the Bratunac health facility, and the 65 ter number is 1892. It is page 26 of the document, the original B/C/S document. The ERN is 0179-3916. This particular page has not been translated. Thank you. If we could scroll down a little bit. Even a little bit more, please. Thank you. Perfect. That's probably as big as we can get without losing the text. Okay. Perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this document before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just hang on a moment, and we'll see if we can get it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to draw your attention to three entries at the bottom of this page. They are numbered 1480, 1481, and 1482. Do you see those entries all the way on the left-hand --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you look -- if you look at the far left side of this document, there's a column with numbers, and you should see "1480","1481," and "1482" running down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All we can see is the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we scroll to the right a little?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Now it's visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Perfect, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you see the column directly to the right of those numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The column with the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you read the date and the time that's listed under each of those dates for those three entries, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the first one is the 12th of the 7th, 1995. The second one -- MS. (redacted): Sorry. Would it be possible to focus a little bit more on the document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we're looking at entry 1480, 1481 and 1482, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. The 14th of the 7, 1995, 4.30. Fourteenth of the 7, 1995, 4 -- it's blurry, the time. It would probably be 4.30. And the 14th of the 7, 1995, 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "14 of the 7, 1995", what do you mean -- how do you read that, sir, to mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you say "4.30" when you look at the times, is that 4.30 in the morning or 4.30 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say this is 4.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving again to your right, in the next column do you see three sets of names? And if you do, would you please read them to yourself - you don't need to read them aloud, and - and I ask you whether you recognise any of those names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the name, but I cannot recognise the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could scroll to the right a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you'll see that the next column has three years, and then the column after that has three, looks like, locations, and then I just want you to read the third column, sir. Can you see what that entry is for the top column or for the top?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Special Brigade Police, Jahorina."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it's the same entry for the next two below it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then what does the next column say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you read that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you scroll up, please, sir, just so we can see what the heading of those two columns is. Can you read the Cyrillic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you focus a bit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it would be the Cyrillic to the far left and the heading next to that one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. The first one is "Unit," and the second one is the place of injury or "Place of wounding," and the next one, "Diagnosis."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, I think everybody here would accept that Sandici is in close proximity to Kravica. Having reviewed this medical log, which indicates that these three Special Police Brigade from Jahorina members were injured in the early morning hours of the 14th of the July, how does that correspond with your recollection of the dates of these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, if those dates are correct, then if we were -- on that point in time, if that's the place where we were, then two days -- a day or two days prior that we have been in Potocari, if that is the -- where are you going with the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think you've answered it about as much as we're going to try to with you, sir. Thank you. Now, sir, you were asked some questions about whether you had any further information about (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the fact he was from (redacted) is something I think that is new, in terms of what you've said to us here in this Tribunal in the last day or so. Let me, if I could, just read a portion of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995. And this is at page 11 of the English, and B/C/S, page 10. There it's written: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were -- whether you provided that information to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, is that information accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the best of my recollection, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I wanted to just ask you a question about the position of 17 (redacted). You said you couldn't remember what his real name was or whether, in fact, you were told his real name. Do you remember what you told -- what you stated in your deposition as to what his actual position was or whether he was a regular Special Police Brigade member or simply a recruit like yourself? Do you remember what you said in the deposition about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm objecting now to this question. I don't believe that this issue of the rank (redacted) was raised during my cross-examination. I did deal with the fact that this person didn't have much details about him. But about the rank, there was nothing that was raised during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I do recall the witness mentioning it earlier on today. Let me just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, maybe I can assist Your Honours. On yesterday's transcript, on page 52, this was the question posed by my colleague, and I believe that the witness already gave his answer. And I never asked anything about (redacted) rank or whether he belonged to regular or special police force or a recruit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, there was some cross-examination which was obviously designed to illicit the witness's lack of knowledge about any of these individuals, and I'm simply looking to see whether his recollection can be refreshed to further identify who these people were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's perfectly in order, so let's proceed with the witness's answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And for the record, sir, I'm going to refer you to page 12 of your deposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's ERN 0149-9695. That's at the bottom of page 9 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were being asked about the structure of your units from Jahorina, and the question was: "And to step up from this fellow recruit, who was the next superior, for example, the company commander?" And your answer was: "It would be the regular guy." The next question: "And do you recall what his name was?" And your answer was: (redacted) When you say the next step up from a recruit like yourself would be "the regular guy," what do you mean by "the regular guy," sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member, a regular member of the police force or special police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. My last question concerns and relates to the questions you were asked about (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we'll need the assistance of Madam Usher, because I don't think this document is in e-court, so we'll need to place it on the ELMO. This is a photograph that has been disclosed to my friends on February 4th, 2007. It is part of Dean Manning's report, ERN 0610-6454 to 0610-0647, disclosed 6 July of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is the Prosecution's position and evidence that (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the photograph in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please clarify that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: (redacted), sir, in the photograph? I just don't know how clear it is for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Witness, before you answer the question. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honours, it is redirect, and the Prosecution is first putting his case to the witness, then asking him to confirm. I mean, this is really inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We all are in agreement with you, Mr. Lazarevic. You either move to something else, Mr. Thayer, or rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, I thank you, and I thank His Worship, and I thank His Worship's staff for their cooperation. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Thayer. Judge Kwon, do you have any questions? Judge Stole? Judge Prost? No questions. Witness, that brings your testimony to an end. We don't have any further questions for you. Before we close this videolink testimony, however, I wish to thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber and the Tribunal for having given evidence, and I also wish to thank you, Magistrate, and your legal officer for attending during the testimony. And if you could also convey, on our behalf, our gratitude to the authorities of your countries for helping in organising this videolink and also the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a good day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that brings to the end the witness. Now we need to proceed with the tendering of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's just one document that we have to offer. Everything else has been already admitted. The one document is the pseudonym sheet, P02878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I won't even ask whether there is any objections. That is so admitted, and it will remain under seal. Mr. Lazarevic, do you wish to tender any documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have two documents to offer. One is 4DP0001. It's the order of President Radovan Karadzic, dated 16 of June, 1995. And the other document is 4D00119. It's a report by the deputy Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objection on your part, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection by the other Defence teams? There is no objection, so the two documents will be admitted, and they will be given the proper identification number. All right. We can now move to the next witness, which, as I understand, is 108, who has come back for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, I am being informed that in order to be able to proceed, because we have been on a videolink connection, they have to make proper readjustments and that they require, at a minimum, about 20 minutes for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we suggest to do is we'll have a 20-minute break now, and then we go straight to the end, with a ten-minute break somewhere, when it becomes either more convenient to you or because of technical reasons. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, and welcome back. We are going to proceed with your testimony now, and you are about to cross-examined by Mr. Bourgon, who is appearing for the Accused Nikolic. May I remind you of the two things I explained to you when you started giving evidence the other day. One is that you are testifying under oath, really, the solemn declaration that you made before you started your testimony. That still applies, holds good. The second is the explanation that I gave you in relation to your right to ask to be exempted from answering some questions, if you feel they are incriminating, incriminatory. All right. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I begin, I would like to know, do we have to stop or can we until a quarter to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I think, at this point, having started at a minute or two after 12:00, I think it would be possible to continue right to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I would prefer, but I just want to know in terms to pace myself with the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, if you need a break, you only have to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I don't think I will need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have quite a bit of questions for you this morning. I will hope to conclude -- I will try to conclude today, my cross-examination. If that is not possible, then I guess we will have to continue tomorrow morning. Before I begin with any substantive questions related to your testimony, I would like to confirm, basically, the general outline of your testimony, which will help me to limit my cross-examination. So correct me if I'm wrong, but in your testimony, you answered questions in respect of three events, and I will go basically over those three events. So the first event you testified about is a visit you allegedly made to the Zvornik Brigade Command with your friend, sometime in July of 1995, so that's the first event you testified about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Of course, this is not the only time you went to Zvornik Brigade Command between the period, let's say, from 1992 to 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that was not your first visit, either, to the Zvornik Brigade Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you mean by "yes" that it was not your first visit? That's my understanding. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was the first visit. The next one was the one I made together with my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I was not clear enough. I'm just talking about going to Zvornik Brigade Command itself. That visit that you testified about was not the first time that you went to the Zvornik Brigade Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time I went to the Command with that friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the second event --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The second event that you spoke about during your testimony would be an alleged second visit to the Zvornik Brigade Command one month later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, thirdly, the other event you spoke about would be an occasion when you met your friend at his house socially several months later, when he spoke to you about a cut-off head he saw near a school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the place where I worked that we socialised, and he observed what I described to you (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies things, because I --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Shall we redact this part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we need to redact part of line 15 and then whatever I said from 17 to 21. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So, Witness, let's go back and simply say that those -- all I want to is clarify with you those three events. So the first one is the alleged visit when you went with your friend to Z Brigade Command, the second one is another Z Brigade Command 30 days later, and the third is a visit where the place where you worked, and that was several months later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to quickly just confirm the general outline of that first visit to the Zvornik Brigade Command. So correct me if I'm wrong, but my understanding is your friend arrived to your location in the morning. He invited you to go to Zvornik Brigade Command. You went there. You had an event that took place at the Z Brigade Command. You returned to your location, and then your friend left for Belgrade. Is that the general outline of that first alleged visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My next question has to do with your knowledge of Commander Pandurevic, because he was the one that you were going to see. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you knew Commander Pandurevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also met him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I just knew of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you knew that Commander Pandurevic had been commander of the Zvornik Brigade for approximately -- well, for over two years; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I knew that he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And it is my understanding that your friend also knew Commander Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would it be correct in saying that your friend had met with Mr. Pandurevic before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that Commander Pandurevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, sorry, and would you agree with me, sir, that Commander Pandurevic was pretty well in control of the Zvornik Brigade in 1995? He was exercising effective control over that brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the point I'm really trying to get at here, sir, is that from your point of view, and I'm not going to say what your work was because we're in public session, but from your professional point of view, would you agree with me that when Commander Pandurevic took over Zvornik Brigade, things changed for the better in the Zvornik area? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic, for assisting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with absolute certainty either way because I wasn't aware how things were unfolding, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I think about Mr. Obrenovic, you would agree with me that you knew Mr. Obrenovic before that visit in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you also met with Mr. Obrenovic on a number of occasions between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but only in the area where I worked. It was socialising between us as private persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But you knew him much more than you knew Commander Pandurevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little better.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if we look at your friend, your friend also knew Mr. Obrenovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I would also say that your friend knew Mr. Obrenovic from 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And your friend had a number of meetings with Mr. Obrenovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just date/year range would be helpful, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it he's still referring to between 1992 and 1995. That's how I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. President. I was referring to the period between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So, Witness, just to clarify things concerning that last question, the question was whether your friend had a number of meetings with Mr. Obrenovic during the period from 1992 to 1995, and your answer was, "Possibly." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, "possibly" is kind of a, I would say, not -- I'd like you to be a bit more precise, because I'm saying a number of meetings, and you say, "Possibly." So they had a number of meetings. How many meetings did they have during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely, considering that I was not there when they met. I can only assume that they met.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But you knew that they did meet at times when you were not there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. I move on to a different topic, and that is -- now we're still in the very general questions before I get into the events themselves, but I'd like to go over your knowledge of Mr. Drago Nikolic. And I'll just refer to what you said in your testimony, whether you can confirm. First of all, that you knew Drago Nikolic before this visit to the Zvornik Brigade Command, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by sight, but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That was my next question, Witness, so that's pretty good, because you testified, in fact, that you knew him by sight, and that was on page 759 of the transcripts at line 10 to 11, and when I say -- would you agree with me that you maybe had seen him two or three times at the most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was there with my friend, I was with him then, and maybe I ran across him in passing, once perhaps, but we didn't socialise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. So I understand from your answer that before this alleged meeting in 1995, you saw him in passing once. Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So I take it, then, that you had never spoken to Drago Nikolic or had a meeting with him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that you, as just said yourself, that you did not socialise. My next point is: What about your friend? I take it that he did not know Mr. Nikolic before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say either way because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you have no recollection whether your friend had ever seen Mr. Drago Nikolic before, or is it that he had never seen him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And given that you had seen Mr. Nikolic just one time in passing before, you don't really know if Mr. Nikolic knew you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that's exactly my point. He might have known you, maybe, as a public figure because of your position, but you don't know whether he knew you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you said in your testimony, at page 761, that you knew that Drago Nikolic was affiliated to the Intelligence Service, and that was before the alleged visit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you said, on page 760, that this was a notorious fact in Zvornik. Can you elaborate on that? What do you mean by "a notorious fact in Zvornik" that Mr. Nikolic was affiliated to the Intelligence Service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose everybody at the Command knew what kind of work Mr. Nikolic was doing; and from the comments of those who worked at the Command, this knowledge spread.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you testified also, on line 24 of the same page, that you "cannot remember the person who told me that," and then you stated that, "I learned from other people at the barracks." Page 759, lines 13-14. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So what did the people tell you at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not at the barracks. It's outside the barracks where I worked. People spoke about the fact that Mr. Nikolic was working for that service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember. It was a long time ago, too long a time for me to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Is it too long a time for you to remember who is it in the barracks that shared that information with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you cannot share with us today the name of anyone from the barracks that you would have met who told you that Mr. Nikolic was affiliated to the Intelligence Service; is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'll move on to -- I've got two more general issues, and then we'll get to more substantive questions. You testified on page 751, lines 1 to 10, yesterday, when you described that first alleged visit. The only thing I'd like to confirm at this time - we will get into the details later - is that when your friend came to see you at your location, he said that -- maybe I should read it just to avoid any misunderstanding. On page 751, I will read what you said yesterday, and that is exactly at line -- first, let's take the question: "If you can remember what, if any, he said about what he was worried about." And your answer was: "My friend said that he was worried and that something was happening across over there." And just to make it clear, to avoid any objection from my colleague, at line 10 you said: "He said that something bad was happening." Do you recall testifying to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that before going to Zvornik Brigade, you did not have any further details as to what is it that your friend was referring to when he mentioned bad things happening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have one last general question before I move to your background, and that is something you mentioned yesterday. And, again, I will quote from the transcript on page 765, and that is the part where you were asked by my colleague whether on the trip back from Zvornik Brigade Command to Mali Zvornik, your friend was able to provide you with any more detail about where these bad things were happening on the basis of that meeting he allegedly had. "Allegedly" is added by me. Your answer was, and I quote on page 765, line 25, and 766, lines 1 to 2: "He just mentioned several schools where prisoners were being kept, but he did not say exactly what was going on at those schools." I stop here for now because the name of the school is something we'll look at later. Do you remember testifying to that effect two days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. What I will do at this point, sir, is I will first have a few questions which relate to your background, and we'll go into private session for that, then I'll move on with some questions with your relationship with the Prosecution over the years, and then we'll go into the alleged visit, itself, just so that you know where I'm going with my cross-examination. Mr. President, if we can go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Looking at your relationship or your dealings with the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal over the years, it is my understanding, sir, that the first time you met with the Prosecution, it had nothing to do with the events which unfolded in 1995. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I don't know if you know the exact date, but I simply suggest to you -- I have an info report which was drafted by the Office of the Prosecution, which dates back to the 27th November 2002. Do you recall meeting with the Prosecution at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And on that occasion, the object of this meeting was to discuss the events which unfolded in the area of Zvornik in the period in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I had the opportunity to read this information report, and my understanding of it, if I can summarise or try to summarise in one sentence and see if you will agree, you told the Prosecution that you were aware of what happened in Zvornik in 1992, but that you were not involved in those events. Would that be a fair summarisation of what you told the Prosecution when you met with them in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that what was generally known and what I could hear from the information media, well, that's what I confirm. What everybody knew, that's what I knew, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And so beyond what the people knew about the events of 1992, you did not have any direct involvement into those events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the next time you met with the Prosecution, based on the information I have, would be on 21 July 2006 in -- at your location. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you recall this interview, which I had the opportunity to read, and maybe we -- we'll go over that interview today. I'm not sure yet. But my understanding is that when you had this interview, someone contacted you before to make an appointment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you share with us today who is it that contacted you and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who contacted me, I think, were the representatives of the Tribunal and the interpreter. He had my number, and he made an appointment, but I can't remember who the person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And how much time was it before the actual interview that you were contacted by the persons you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it might have been a few days, up to a month. I'm not quite sure.
