utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did they tell you what they wanted to discuss with you during this interview and why they were contacting you, yourself? Because you had spoken to them before, so what did they tell you this interview would be about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't say, but I accepted to talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that when they met with you, they never mentioned your friend, or did they mention your friend when they called you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that you must have asked them, "Why is it that you want to speak to me?" Did you say that, or did you just accept blindly any invitation by people from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accepted because I considered it to be my civic duty, and I didn't lay down any conditions, nor did I ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I take it that the next time you met with the Prosecution was not until the 14th of June of this year, when you came for the first time to testify in this case. Do you recall coming here on the 14th of June of this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you were supposed to testify at that moment, and you did not because of a request from the Defence, because we needed more time to investigate and also because we had just received a lot of information, additional information, by the Prosecution which concerned you. Were you informed of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They informed me, with respect to the Defence, that my testimony had been postponed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did they inform you that they had provided information to the Defence which related to you and that is why we had requested the delay? Did they say that to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly what was said, specifically, but I think they informed me that the Defence had requested a postponement of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. On this occasion, sir, I take it that you did have the opportunity to read your interview - that's the interview of 21 July 2006 - and that you had the opportunity to read this interview in your own language. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you read this -- having read this interview, I take it that, from the information I have, that you did some minor corrections; for example, maybe you recall saying something about the apartment of Commander Pandurevic. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also said, because I have the information here with me, according to the notes I've received from the Prosecution, you would have said that -- you were asked, actually, whether you recall the exact title of Drago Nikolic in the summer of 1995. And you stated that you did not know the exact title, but that you knew he was in Intelligence. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So other than this -- the information you provided to the Prosecution on that day, that is to say, that your interview, you had an opportunity to read it and you answered a couple of questions, I take it that there was nothing knew that came out of this meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the next time you came to the Tribunal, again you were supposed to testify, and my understanding is that this time it was around mid-July 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: All I'm trying to confirm at this point, sir, is whether you did come to The Hague, in July, another time before this week.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came just once and now again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to confirm this, because initially you were scheduled to testify, I think, around mid-July, and it was postponed. Were you informed of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was here that time and I was supposed to testify, the Prosecution informed me that the Defence had requested that I don't testify. So I went back to my place of residence, and now I've come back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies things. Now, in the middle, did you make any travel arrangements at any point to testify again that would have been cancelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that. I don't actually understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to make it as simple as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we know why the question was a little confusing, given how these arrangements are made. I mean, we can provide clarification for that kind of information, if my friend really wants it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon. If this issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My point, Mr. President, is for him, whether he knows. That's what's important to me, whether he knew that there was another scheduling for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, I'll try to explain that to you in very simple terms. You said that you came here once and it was postponed and you returned home, and you said that you came this week and now you are testifying. In between the two, were you informed that you were supposed to come to The Hague to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I returned, while I was returning, I was told that I would be invited to come again to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move on to something else. When you came this week, I take it that you had a meeting with the Prosecution, and that was last Sunday on the 2nd of September. Do you recall meeting with the Prosecution on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And it is my understanding that you were again shown a copy of your interview and that you had a chance to read it in your own language. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And my next question is: Were you shown any other material on that occasion when you met with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just shown a photograph and asked to identify some people, and the day before yesterday I confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you say "the day before yesterday," is that a second meeting you had with the Prosecution or is that at the same meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on Sunday, Sunday. On Sunday, I had contacts, and the day before yesterday I confirmed this on the photograph that I was shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. For me, my purpose is simply to confirm that you met with the Prosecution and you were shown your testimony, you were shown a picture, and you only met with the Prosecution once. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I mention this because we always get proofing notes following any meeting you have with the Prosecution in order to allow us to prepare, and I believe it is important that you are made aware that we have what is discussed between you and the Prosecution before you testify. And the only thing I'd like to say is that, during that meeting on Sunday, would you agree with me that very little, if any, new information came out? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there weren't any. I just read through the transcript and confirmed what was there, that I understood, and there were no additional questions, except to show me the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it, based on the information I have here, that you also at this meeting, you recognised Nikolic. You said that was because of his hair, his distinctive hair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And correct me if I'm wrong, but you also stated on that occasion, two more details; the first one being that the alleged meeting between your friend and Mr. Nikolic took place upstairs at Standard, and that it may have been in the commander or the deputy commander's office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whose office it was, but it wasn't that of Commander Pandurevic or Obrenovic. It wasn't their office. It was quite a different office. I don't know whose office it actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that you know where the office of Commander Pandurevic and the office of the deputy commander is. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Because according to the information I have, it says here it may have been in the commander or deputy commander's office. Can you clarify this for me, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say that. I didn't say that at all. It's quite a different office. When you go up the stairs onto the floor above, the office was to your left, the first door to your left, but we looked for Mr. Pandurevic on the right, where his office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'll just leave it at that. But I also say that it was the first time that you ever provided any information concerning which office this alleged meeting took place in. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, I explained where the meeting was held between myself [as interpreted], my friend, and Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, we'll get back to that, but I'm saying that before that -- well, okay. First let's make a correction in the transcript. I believe, if I read page 68, lines 12 and 13, it says: "The first time, I explained where the meeting was held between myself, my friend, and Mr. Nikolic." First, I'd like to confirm that you were not in that office when your friend spoke to Mr. Nikolic, as you testified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So just now that we take this maybe slip of the tongue away from the equation, you say that you said the first time where the meeting was held. Now, what I'm saying to you today is that based on the information that I have, you were asked that question before, but you never said and never indicated any area precisely or any office where that meeting was held. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question was asked, but I didn't know whose office it was. All I know is that it wasn't Mr. Pandurevic's office or Mr. Obrenovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the fact that it says here in the proofing note that it may have been the commander or deputy commander's office is a mistake that was done by the Prosecution; that's your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it's a mistake. All I know is that I did not say that it was in Mr. Pandurevic's or Mr. Obrenovic's office. It wasn't there. It was in another office. I don't know whose office that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, another thing you said when you met with the Prosecution on that time, you said, prior to 1995, your friend told you that Nikolic was involved in intelligence and security. Did you say that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't put it that way. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you don't know if it's a mistake, but you never said that your friend told you that Nikolic was involved in intelligence and security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about that, as I told you, but my friend didn't comment to me on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'll move on to a different question. But, of course, that information will be part of the record, just so at least we know that you today are saying something different than what I have on this information which was provided to me by the Prosecution. Let me move to a different topic or simply just close on this issue. I want to know whether you have, in your possession, a copy of your interview in your language. Did you ever have this in your possession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't got one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Did you at any time were given a copy to bring home, or here for a couple of days to keep with you, to prepare for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just when I came last time and this time again, I read through it. I was given the opportunity of reading through it several times, but I didn't take it away with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'll move to a different series of questions, and, basically, I'd like to ask you a few things about the events which took place in 1992. As I mentioned previously, you did meet with the Prosecution on 27 November 2002 to discuss these events. You've already said "yes" to this question, but what I need to do at this time, so that the Trial Chamber understands those events which I will cover in my cross-examination, I would like to confirm some of the basic facts which I believe you are aware of and that are established. The first one is that: You are aware that an attack was conducted on Zvornik on the 8th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when the war began or the conflict in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And these are established facts, so it shouldn't be a problem for you to confirm that many units were involved in this attack on 8 April 1992, including units of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik, which were commanded by Branko Popovic, or his other name, Marko Pavlovic, and other paramilitary units such as Arkan's units. So you're aware of these facts, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the participation of Arkan's units, but I don't know under whose command they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you're aware this attack was conducted pursuant to a plan which was adopted by the Serbian Democratic Party, the SDS, which wanted to take over the municipality of Zvornik to chase out the Muslim population and to proclaim this territory as a Serbian municipality; are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if I look at the information report, which contains what you said to the Prosecution on 27 November 2002, let's begin maybe with some of the main players involved. It's my understanding from that report that you know who Branko, or is it Brano, Grujic is, as well as the position he held at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if I tell you, at the time, Brano Grujic was the president of the Serbian Democratic Party, SDS, president of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, and that he became the president of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik War Staff in April 1992, these facts are accurate, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how the public was informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to inform, before I get an objection from the Prosecution, these questions have to do with the credibility of the witness. I need to establish these facts before I go into any substantive question, and I will be done shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, let me continue and say that pursuant to the information report that I have, you knew Brano Grujic very well before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, what about Branko Popovic? You know him, and you know who he is; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-108 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him under the name of "Marko Pavlovic," and (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me that during the conflict, of course, you just mentioned is a.k.a., or his "also known as," name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm a little concerned about the identification of the location at that page. I just simply ask for a redaction, if anybody is familiar with that individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President, and I think we should move into closed session for the next two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll redact that, and we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime, please, same accommodation as before, don't discuss or allow anyone to discuss with you the subject of your testimony. You can escort the witness out, because I see Mr. Thayer on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just a scheduling question, Mr. President, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I was going to ask that myself. May I have, before I give you "la parole," Mr. Thayer, how much more do you reckon you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had announced three hours, and I will need a little more than that, so I figure tomorrow I will need the first session and at least half the second session. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we'll try to keep it below an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's all I wanted to know, because the rest is -- okay. Okay. So we'll continue tomorrow morning. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I was just wondering if we could have an idea of how much of that time we're going to spend in 1992, if we have an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would prefer to keep surprises, but it's my pleasure to inform my colleague I will about maybe 15 or 20 minutes at the most in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And they all have to do with credibility, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: 1992, yes. The rest is also credibility, but in a different regard with the events of 1995. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
